title: SummitWare - inference model & deployment scoping
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment
summary: Discovery call to understand SummitWare's inference needs: high context windows for long-doc summarization, multilingual support (EN/ES/DE/FR), and tool-calling for internal data retrieval. Discussed tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private VPC/on-prem options. SE to run two-model perf/latency benchmark with sample prompts; AE to follow up with security pack and pricing ranges.
next_steps: Ethan to run perf benchmarks (Llama 2 70B quant vs Mistral/Redwood-verified) with SummitWare sample prompts and share results (due 2026-10-26)
Maya to send security docs (SOC2 + Private deployment checklist) and draft pricing scenarios by 2026-10-22
Schedule follow-up deep-dive on VPC networking with Noah (provision 60 minutes) for week of 2026-10-26
action_items: Ethan Brooks: run perf tests with 8k and 32k context prompts using SummitWare corpus; include p95 latency and tokens/sec - due 2026-10-26
Maya Chen: send Redwood Dedicated vs Private one-pager + security pack (SOC2, ISO cert references, KMS options) - due 2026-10-22
Noah Reed: share current VPC topology and egress constraints with Redwood (email) - due 2026-10-21
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-19 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~58 min | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Aisha (SummitWare CTO), Liam (ML Eng), Noah (Cloud Arch)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick intros?
[00:06] Aisha (SummitWare): Hi all, I'm Aisha, CTO at SummitWare. We build long-form analytics summarization for enterprise docs, and we're exploring inference options.
[00:13] Liam (SummitWare): Liam here, ML eng, working on prompt engineering and retrieval.
[00:17] Noah (SummitWare): Noah, infra, I'll be the main contact for networking / VPC constraints.
[00:22] Maya: Great. Ethan, do you want to set the agenda?
[00:25] Ethan (Redwood): Yeah, we'll cover model candidates (open models), context/window needs, multilingual support, tool-calling / retrieval integration, and deployment options — quick Q/A at the end.
[00:33] Aisha: Sounds good. To kick off, our biggest pain right now is we have a bunch of 25k token legal docs, need to produce structured summaries and Q&A. Latency target is p95 < 2s for extractive tasks? but we know tradeoffs exist. Cost is a major concern too.
[00:48] Ethan: Right. Two axes to consider: model choice + runtime. For context: are you doing concatenation + retrieval or windowed streaming?
[00:56] Liam: We do a retrieve-and-construct pipeline: retrieve top k chunks, then feed to chain-of-thought style prompts. Typical prompt after retrieval is ~18k tokens, occasionally up to ~28k.
[01:10] Ethan: Ok so you need >16k but often 32k headroom. We recommend profiling with both 16k-optimized and 32k-optimized variants. For open models, candidates are Llama 2 (70B), Mistral 7B Instruct-ish, and some trimmed Mistral 8k/30k variants — depending on quantization.
[01:29] Aisha: We're also multilingual — English plus Spanish and German primarily. Any models you see better for that?
[01:36] Ethan: Mistral derivatives have good multilingual coverage but Llama 2 70B fine-tuned variants often outperform for complex reasoning. There's also the new open mix models; we can test both. Important note: Redwood's runtime supports KV caching and prefix cache, but that can be tricky when you change context windows — sometimes the transcriber's spelled KV cache as K V cash — heh
[01:57] Liam: hah, yeah. We also want to do tool-calling to query an internal vector DB and a docs API. How do you handle that securely?
[02:05] Maya: Two options: Hosted API with encrypted at-rest and in-transit, or Dedicated/Private where your data never leaves your VPC. For tool-calling, we can support function-style calls and structured JSON outputs; SEs can show typical patterns.
[02:20] Noah: Our security team is strict — prefer Private for PII-sensitive data. But dedicated reserved capacity might be acceptable if we can get enough isolation and contractual guarantees.
[02:31] Ethan: Totally. Dedicated gives you pinned GPU pools and isolation at the tenant layer; Private gives you a control plane in your VPC or an on-prem bundle. We do integrate with KMS for key management and audit logs are available for both.
[02:45] Aisha: One of our constraints is token cost — we don't want the cost to spiral compared to our internal self-hosting experiments. Do you have tooling to reduce unit cost?
[02:54] Ethan: Yes — batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization profiles and routing policies. For long-document summarization, prefix caching doesn't help as much since prompts vary, but smart rerouting to smaller models for summarization-only tasks can drop cost dramatically. We can show model routing rules: e.g., cheap summarizer (7B quant) for extractive summaries and 70B for deep Q&A.
[03:15] Liam: How about latency for 32k tokens on a 70B quantized model? We measured in-house around p95 9-12s on A100-ish setups.
[03:24] Ethan: That aligns. Our numbers depend on compilation/kernels; on Redwood Dedicated we target 6-10s p95 for 32k on optimized 70B with int8 quant and batch size 1, but it varies. We'll run your samples to get exacts.
[03:36] Aisha: Great. Can the Hosted API do tool-calling with a VPC connector?
[03:41] Maya: We have a VPC peering option for Hosted that allows secure egress to your services, but it's not as isolated as Private. For strict egress control and no internet access we recommend Private.
[03:52] Noah: If we go Private, what's the installation footprint? We have an air-gapped option?
[03:56] Ethan: Private can be deployed in your VPC or on-prem. On-prem air-gapped is supported but requires additional ops work — we'll share the checklist. For cloud VPC we provide a control plane connectivity pattern and agents inside your VPC.
[04:10] Aisha: How do you handle multi-region data residency — we have EU customers.
[04:15] Maya: We offer region pinning and routing policies. Dedicated capacity can be provisioned in region; Private obviously runs where you host it. We'll include a region/residency note in the security pack.
[04:26] Liam: Back to models — how do you recommend evaluating model quality for multilingual docs?
[04:31] Ethan: Two-prong: run automated evals (BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics for translation/summaries) and human evals for critical cases. We can run a narrow eval harness with your test set across 3 models and return ROUGE, hallucination rates, and example breakdowns.
[04:47] Aisha: Good. Also, we sometimes need tool-calling that triggers external API calls (billing systems) — can those function calls be audited?
[04:55] Maya: Yes — we log function invocations, request payloads per retention policy, and can export audit logs to your SIEM. For Private you control retention.
[05:05] Noah: From a networking POV, we need to know egress ports, IAM roles, and whether there's a way to route via our proxy.
[05:12] Ethan: We'll get you a networking doc: required ports (TLS 443 for control plane, gRPC endpoints), recommended IAM roles for agents, and proxy patterns.
[05:21] Aisha: Okay next, pricing — can you ballpark Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
[05:25] Maya: Ballpark: Hosted is usage-based (per-token + per-embedding). Dedicated is reserved monthly capacity with lower per-token cost and SLA. Private has platform licensing + support and higher upfront. We'll send ranges and a sample TCO using your projected monthly tokens.
[05:39] Liam: For benchmarking, what artifacts do you need?
[05:42] Ethan: A set of 20 representative prompts, 10 heavy-context examples (20-32k), and target metrics (p95 latency, tokens/sec, accuracy). If you can share sanitized samples or hashes, that'll work.
[05:56] Aisha: We'll sanitize and share by Friday.
[05:58] Maya: Great. We'll plan perf runs and follow up with security docs. Any other questions?
[06:02] Noah: One last: can you show the routing fallback — like if Dedicated capacity is saturated, automatic fallback to hosted?
[06:09] Ethan: Yes — we have smart routing policies and automatic model fallback chains. We'll include an example: prefer dedicated 70B, fallback to hosted 70B-quant or smaller 7B route depending on policy.
[06:21] Aisha: Nice.
[06:23] Maya: Ok recap: Ethan runs perf tests (due 10/26) with your samples; Maya sends security & pricing (due 10/22); Noah shares VPC topology (due 10/21). We'll schedule a follow-up deep-dive for VPC/networking next week.
[06:36] Liam: Sounds good, thanks.
[06:38] Aisha: Thanks, bye.

Notes (auto-summary): occasional transcription errors present ("K V cash" for KV cache, "Redwood Dedicates" for Dedicated), speaker overlaps minimal.

End of transcript.
